multiPersonaRules: No modes to choose: no simple/expert switch and no persona picker. One app serves everyone through progressive disclosure: summary → Details fold → technical page.

Write the defaults for the newcomer and keep everything reachable for the tinkerer. Primary surfaces use the person's words only; engine words, ids, paths and addresses live under Details, in mono, copyable (ui_glossary_test).

Context chooses, not the person. Actions follow what the server is and what it can do (ServerCapabilities, never the flavour enum): a phone server gets Restart and cost lines; a remote server gets network help and a server switch.
Automation is the default and manual controls are the fallback. Automatic actions are announced afterwards in one line with Undo where possible; manual levers sit in row menus or overflow.
Remember choices instead of re-asking: supervision, project, model, new-conversation mode and delivery (Queue) per server.

Ask for consent once, in the flow, at the moment it matters (battery exemption, auto-approve, auto-merge, background checks, large downloads on mobile data). Never make the person hunt for it in Settings.

Where tinkerer detail lives: (a) the Details fold at the bottom of a KitStateView or sheet; (b) the row's KitRowMenu; (c) technical pages reached from Settings › Diagnostics or a server's details, never inside a primary flow; (d) keyboard shortcuts and the command palette. Tool pages (processes, logs, team-run tabs) may be dense.

A missing capability explains itself instead of vanishing. Today 285 whenMissing gates are 'hidden', against 18 that offer to enable. Where a person could enable a feature, show one row: 'Not on this server · why · Turn it on'.
One job, one landing place. The same job started from anywhere ends on the same page (Give the team a task vs Solo · Team; Add server vs Connect OpenCode 2).
Density follows the page's role: glance pages (Work, Inbox, Team home) get one line per item; work pages (chat, review) put content first; tool pages may be dense.
The cross-cutting needs (200 % text, TalkBack, Arabic RTL, one hand, slow network) are enforced by tests and goldens, not left to review, and apply to every persona.

verticals.standard: Every screen is built from lib/ui/kit (the design_standard_test migrated list only grows): one confirm, one sheet frame, one log view, one row anatomy, at most one primary. Destructive actions are always error-coloured and confirmed. Motion comes only from KitMotion.

worst.issue: the reference shape, yet at least eight AlertDialog confirmations bypass it; KitConfirmSheet is proposed on 78 elements
mostly hand-built; kit only for request cards, skeleton and status line
four Scaffolds in one 3265-line file
destructive in green (also profile-editor-discard-sheet, provider-quota-clear-dialog, usage-budget-clear-dialog)
three notice-line implementations stack; embedded-product-states is why the app has two error styles

mechanisms: New kit parts, ranked by the kitGap counts in the map: KitConfirmSheet (78), KitSheet (33), KitSegmented (15), KitLogPanel (13), KitChoiceRow (11), KitSearchField (10), KitCommandBlock (8), KitInputDialog (7), KitDetailsFold (7), KitDiscardGuard (3).
Gate: design_standard_test bans AlertDialog, ListTile, ExpansionTile, SwitchListTile and raw progress in migrated screens; team_design_standard_test likewise.
Goldens in dark and light for every migrated screen.

verticals.standard: Never lose typed work (check X2, principle 10). Nothing typed, dictated, queued or attached is lost on back, swipe-down, crash, force stop or a lost server. Sheets with input keep a draft instead of asking. Queued prompts are never deleted silently.

worst.issue: the team objective is lost on swipe (critical); owner: 'Give the user recovery options?'
a typed comment is lost on swipe (critical)
a typed message is discarded on swipe (critical); team-board-add-sheet, gate-sheet and the team-conversation composer too
unapplied edits lost on back (critical); development-services-editor-sheet likewise
an unsent transcript is discarded; form-sheet answers are lost on back; servers-remove-server-sheet deletes queued prompts silently

mechanisms: Kit: KitDiscardGuard wraps any sheet with input and keeps the draft silently (restores on reopen) instead of a confirm.
Service: DraftStore keyed oc.draft.<target>.<profileId> (swept by ProfileStore.profileScopedPreferenceKeys).
Gate: a harness test that opens every input sheet, types, swipes it down, reopens it and asserts the text is kept.

verticals.standard: Before and after work, the person can see what it costs in money or tokens (per turn and per team task) and how close they are to a quota or budget. A default alert fires at 80 %. Device cost is covered under battery-heat.

worst.issue: five type sizes; '30 days' vs 'Sep 2-6'
team-wide cost shown as the agent's
nothing says which model is cheap or fast
no last-known result offline
no time or cost expectation before creating a cloud sandbox

mechanisms: A CostService per turn, task and provider, feeding KitCostLine and the conversation header.
Default budget alert at 80 %, with the threshold suggested from last month.
Model rows carry a plain price tier.

verticals.standard: A person with several servers (laptop, phone, Claude Code) sees what needs them on all of them, answers without switching, and every item names its server.

worst.issue: other servers' state is missing
must switch servers to answer a request
does not say which server a request comes from
reachability is not shown
a link that names a server cannot add it and resume

mechanisms: A gateway per profile, so a request is answered in place.
One Needs-you inbox across servers, oldest first.
Kit: a server chip on rows, cards and notifications.

verticals.standard: 'Don't have X, want X': a feature that needs a missing capability says why it is off and offers the enable flow. It never silently vanishes.

worst.issue: gated rows vanish silently
silently shrinks on Codex/Paseo (also command-launcher-sheet, prompt-tools-sheet)
no path from 'no models' to signing in
no path to enable
sends the person to Settings instead of installing through v2

mechanisms: A capability-explainer registry: capability id → reason and enable flow (offers-enable:<flow>).
Kit: KitCapabilityRow.
Gate: a map audit asserting that whenMissing 'hidden' is used only where no enable flow exists.

auto: Connection: reconnect with backoff and a visible countdown ('trying again in 10 s'); re-probe health on connectivity change; retry share or link intake once the connection returns.
Queued prompts: reconcile each send with the server transcript after reconnect (delivered or not) without asking; auto-retry a provider-overloaded failure with backoff and say so.

Phone server: start on tap when stopped; restart after an Android force stop or crash (built, not device-proven); resume setup after a kill, reboot or network return; re-check Termux, Tailscale and sign-in on app resume; poll health after a restart until the new version answers.
Heat: pause the phone's AI Team at SEVERE and resume after 2 cool minutes (built, on by default); drop Effects to Calm or solid under battery saver or heat.

Defaults instead of questions: open the only or last-used project; create 'my-app' on first run; show the server's default model by name; choose the voice pack from total RAM and the read-aloud voice from the locale; Queue rather than Steer; open the review scope that has changes; Split only at ≥600 dp; generate names and titles from the first prompt; skip a picker with one option (shell, provider, project).
Detection: the server kind after pairing (OpenCode 1/2, Paseo); a team host on the paired computer; existing installs via v2 check scripts.
Data safety: keep drafts per target instead of asking; attach a recovered photo to its own draft; restore a saved prompt at once with Undo.

Live views: follow logs and output while at the bottom; poll while open; page near the end (bounded); pages follow the controller with no refresh buttons (team-run, team-agents, embedded-team-cycle-strip).

Team housekeeping: the dispatcher routes ready work to free workers; wake a stalled pool or nudge after its window, then say so; restart a crashed worker; recycle at the context threshold; hold a worker at a provider limit until reset; retry an unconfirmed answer once; re-sling a transiently failed step once; fall back to a direct task when the planner is off.
App updates: download the code push silently, apply it at the next cold start, say so once.
consentOnce: Keep running: the battery-optimisation exemption and the maker's auto-start/lock screen, asked in flow when the phone's server first starts (keep-running guidance exists).
Notifications permission with the preset 'Tell me when the agent needs me'.
Auto-approval: after 3 identical asks, offer 'Always allow this' (for this conversation or server) on the request card itself.
Supervision level for the AI Team, remembered per server. Under Balanced or Autonomous it is the consent to auto-approve and auto-merge when checks pass; under High, merges stay manual.

Housekeeping with side effects: restart dev services on crash, stop leftover helpers after 10 min idle, clean regenerable caches when space is low, update Termux or OpenCode when idle (never mid-reply).
Background monitoring of other servers and provider quota (battery and data cost stated; Wi-Fi-only option).
Large downloads on mobile data (>50 MB: voice models, Ubuntu, AI Team), asked once per network type.
The agent assistant running commands on the server to set up MCP, configuration or the AI Team (the first time, with what it will run).
Including diagnostics in a problem report (a preview is shown every time).
Keeping a warm AI Team worker (~550 MB RAM, one process), after the device experiment proves it idles quietly.
manual: Anything irreversible or outward-facing: delete a project, the Ubuntu install, a server's data or a conversation; apply a revert or staged revert; reset or remove a worktree; public share links; remove credentials; switch organisation.
Decisions the agent asks for outside saved rules: permissions, questions, forms, supervision gates, merges under High supervision.
Choosing what to build: the task objective, the prompt, starting a team task.
Signing in: OAuth, API keys, device codes. Credentials are never automated or echoed.
Running an ad-hoc shell command, or stopping a running command or process.
Tinkerer levers, kept in overflow as fallbacks with what automation already did shown beside them: nudge, reassign, restart, stop, per-agent pause, manual refresh, manual address entry.
needsYouContract: Interrupt only for (1) a decision only the person can make: a permission outside their saved rules, a question or form, a gate their supervision reserves, a merge under High supervision.

(2) Work that cannot continue without them: credentials expired or rejected, a provider limit or budget reached with no fallback, storage full blocking work, or a step still failing after automatic retries (say what was tried).
(3) A first-time consent from the consent-once list, at the moment it becomes relevant, never before.

Every Needs-you item says why, what happens if it is ignored ('the team waits; nothing is lost'), and can be answered in one tap from the notification. It is deduplicated, oldest first, names its server, and disappears everywhere once answered elsewhere.

Never a Needs-you: reconnecting, restarts, heat pauses, updates, finished work, progress. These go on quiet status lines (KitStatusLine/KitNotice) and, if backgrounded, the quiet status channel. They are collected in 'While you were away'.
'Done' notifications are opt-in per task type (default on for team tasks and long runs) and are not interruptions.
